maximumProof.degreeReduction: For deg(g)=d>=2, deg((g-x)^2)=2d >= d+2=deg(x^2*g-8), impossible for a Euclidean remainder. Constant g also fails the strict remainder-degree condition. Thus g=ux+v with u!=0 and Q=(4/u)x+s.
maximumProof.rootAssignment: Because g and Q are nonzero linear polynomials and (x-1)(x-2) divides gQ, one has roots 1 and 2 split between them. The assignment g(2)=0,Q(1)=0 violates |g(1)|<|g(2)|. Thus g(1)=0,Q(2)=0, so v=-u and s=-8/u.
maximumProof.coefficientReduction: Writing f=2x^2+px+r, coefficient comparison in f^2+7(g-x)^2=(x^2*g-8)Q yields p=-3, r=-(1+7(u-1)^2)/4, and 7u^3+14u^2-24u-64=0=(u-2)(7u^2+28u+32). The quadratic factor has discriminant -112, so the only real possibility is u=2. The constant coefficient equation then holds with v=-2,s=-4,r=-2.
maximumProof.uniqueness: Every feasible real tuple is the displayed witness, so the feasible set is nonempty and its requested value is exactly 9; therefore its maximum is 9.
